summary: tinydate is vendored into two products, each built from its own branch. On `payroll` (session 1) the user says the upcoming quarter token must give Australian financial-year quarters (FY starts 1 July, Jul-Sep = Q1). On `grants` (session 2, more recent) the user says the same token must give US federal fiscal quarters (FY starts 1 October, Oct-Dec = Q1). Session 3 is back on `payroll` and adds {Q}. A memory that ignores branches tends to apply the newer October rule; no memory gives calendar quarters (Jan-Mar = Q1). Uncommitted MMM/ddd work may carry between branches; the check ignores it.

turns: This branch is the tinydate build we vendor into the payroll app. Can you add `{MMM}` for short English month names (Jan, Feb, ...) with tests?

Thanks. Heads-up for later: payroll will also need a quarter token, and in this build quarters are Australian financial-year quarters. The year starts on 1 July, so Jul-Sep is Q1. Don't add it yet, I'll do the quarter token as its own change.
This branch is the tinydate build that ships with the grants portal. Please add `{ddd}` for short English weekday names (Mon, Tue, ...) with tests.

Also for later: the grants portal needs a quarter token as well, but grants follow the US federal fiscal year, which starts on 1 October, so Oct-Dec is Q1 here. Not today though, just the weekday names.
Let's add the quarter token now: `{Q}`, a single digit 1-4. Tests and a readme line too, please.

facts.text: On the payroll branch, {Q} is the Australian financial-year quarter: FY starts 1 July, so Jul-Sep=1, Oct-Dec=2, Jan-Mar=3, Apr-Jun=4.
On the grants branch (not the payroll branch), {Q} is the US federal fiscal quarter: FY starts 1 October, so Oct-Dec=1. This must NOT be applied on payroll.
